title: Operator Sentinel, Escrow Artifacts, and Durable Rollback Procedures for Private Deploys
author: Marceline Chen
content:
Overview

This runbook defines the operational pattern we call the Operator Sentinel + Escrow strategy: an explicit, reproducible process for taking escrowed artifacts and operator signals as inputs to a safe, auditable rollback for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers what to capture (escrow artifacts), when operator automation should trigger a rollback versus a mitigative mode, and the detailed step-by-step manual and automated rollback procedures for both stateless and stateful systems (model artifacts, KV caches, runtime state).

Why this doc exists

- Private deployments require reversible operations that preserve customer state and compliance evidence.
- Rollbacks must be deterministic, minimize data loss, and provide verifiable evidence for audits.
- Operators in the field need clear, short checklists and reproducible commands to perform durable rollbacks with minimal risk.

Scope

Applies to: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) control plane operator actions, runtime model swaps, model artifact installations, KV-cache migrations, and configuration rollouts affecting tenant traffic. Does NOT replace full disaster recovery procedures (see related DR playbooks).

Owner and escalation

- Primary owner: Platform Ops (engineering).
- Secondary owner: Private Deploy Customer Success.
- Oncall escalation: private-deploys-sre -> eng-sre -> eng-platform lead.

Operational definitions and primitives

- Sentinel: A short-lived operator process (automation or human-observed metric) that evaluates SLOs and forensic signals to classify a rollout as OK / degraded / unsafe. The sentinel runs in the operator namespace and posts outcomes to the operator-event-log.
- Escrow artifact: Immutable snapshot(s) produced before any material change. Examples: model-artifact-signed.tar.gz checksum, KV-cache-snapshot (leveldb/rocksdb/redis RDB), runtime-config-manifest.yaml, tenant-state-delta.tar.gz.
- Durable rollback: A rollback process that guarantees the original pre-change state is restorable without data corruption and with preserved evidence for auditing.

Escrow artifact policy (required)

Before any operator-initiated change that is non-trivial (model swap, quantization change, runtime binary upgrade, KV cache migration):

1) Create escrow bundle and place it in the escrow store (customer-specific S3/GCS bucket or onprem NFS mount). Required components:
   - control-plane-manifest.yaml (git-ref + commit SHA)
   - model-artifact-{model-name}-{version}.tar.gz (signed, sha256)
   - model-metadata.json (tokenizer hash, layer_count, sequence_length_limits)
   - kv-cache-snapshot-{timestamp}.rdb (if applicable)
   - operator-log-{change-id}.ndjson (events leading to the change)
   - acceptance-synthetics-{change-id}.tar.gz (synthetic traces used in canary)

2) Record escrow metadata in the operator registry: change-id, escrow-uri, operator, started_at. Example CLI:

   redwood operator escrow create --change-id=chg-2026-1123 \
     --escrow-uri=s3://customer-escrow/rw-escrow/chg-2026-1123.tgz \
     --manifest=control-plane-manifest.yaml \

3) Validate signatures and checksums. If any signature check fails, abort.

Sentinel triggers and thresholds (suggested defaults)

- Error rate: frontend request error rate > 1.5% sustained for 10m -> sentinel enters degraded.
- Latency regressions: p50 > 150ms or p95 > 400ms over baseline -> degraded.
- Token rejection: model request rejection rate > 0.2% -> unsafe.
- Throughput drop: >= 30% reduction in sustained throughput for 5m -> degraded.
- Customer-facing SLA breach: any availability drop that touches an SLA boundary -> unsafe.

The sentinel supports tunable window sizes per-customer. Production defaults above are used unless the customer contract specifies tighter bounds.

Decision matrix (short)

- OK: sentinel reports green -> continue rollout.
- Degraded: sentinel reports yellow -> pause rollout and run mitigations (traffic-steer to safe model variant, increase autoscale cap, apply KV-cache warmup). If mitigations fail in 30 minutes -> rollback.
- Unsafe: sentinel reports red (SLA breach or token rejections) -> immediate rollback.

Rollback types and safe ordering

We distinguish three rollback families with recommended safe ordering to minimize data loss:

A) Configuration rollback (stateless controls, routing, feature flags)
   - Fastest and lowest risk. No data restore.
   - Procedure: revert manifests, restart routing proxies, validate traffic split.

B) Model artifact rollback (model binary/tensor weights, quantization profiles)
   - Medium risk. Can be stateful if the runtime persisted a KV cache tied to the model.
   - Procedure: restore model artifact from escrow, restart model worker with version pin, warm KV cache from snapshot where necessary.

C) Stateful runtime rollback (KV cache, session stores, ephemeral runtime artifacts)
   - Highest risk. Needs snapshot coordination and, in certain cases, tenant quiescence.
   - Procedure: coordinate tenant quiesce -> restore KV snapshots -> validate consistency -> resume traffic.

Durable rollback checklist (operator-facing)

1) Confirm change-id and escrow URI (operator registry).
2) Ensure oncall is paged and a single operator is designated to run the rollback.
3) If stateful rollback: request customer or sandbox tenant quiesce window (see tenant-quiesce template).
4) Fetch escrow bundle and verify signatures + checksums.
5) Run pre-restore verification script (see examples below).
6) Execute rollback in the recommended order (see below).
7) Run acceptance synthetics against customer test traffic (5–15 minutes).
8) Capture evidence: operator-log, synthetic results, telemetry export. Attach to the incident ticket.
9) If rollback fails, escalate to eng-platform lead and follow the cross-tenant mitigation playbook.

Example commands and snippets

Fetch and validate escrow (example):

  # fetch bundle (requires operator credentials)
  redwood operator escrow fetch --change-id=chg-2026-1123 --dest=/tmp/chg-1123

  # verify checksum and signature
  sha256sum /tmp/chg-1123/model-artifact-foo-1.2.3.tar.gz
  redwood crypto verify --keyring=/etc/redwood/keys/operator-keyring.kbx \
    /tmp/chg-1123/model-artifact-foo-1.2.3.tar.gz.sig

Restore model artifact (example):

  # push model to local content-store and pin service
  scp /tmp/chg-1123/model-artifact-foo-1.2.3.tar.gz operator@edge-node:/var/lib/redwood/models/
  ssh operator@edge-node 'sudo systemctl stop redwood-model-worker && \
    tar -xzf /var/lib/redwood/models/model-artifact-foo-1.2.3.tar.gz -C /opt/redwood/models && \
    sudo systemctl start redwood-model-worker --version=1.2.3'

KV-cache snapshot restore (redis example):

  # stop writes at the proxy layer (graceful quiesce)
  curl -X POST https://operator.internal/tenants/quiesce -d '{"tenant": "t-123", "duration_s": 600}' \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN'

  # restore RDB into local redis
  cp /tmp/chg-1123/kv-cache-snapshot-20260322.rdb /var/lib/redis/dump.rdb
  sudo systemctl restart redis

  # verify keys count
  redis-cli DBSIZE

Safe restart ordering (recommended)

1) Control-plane manifests (config maps, operator feature-flags)
2) Routing and ingress (proxy) changes
3) Model worker binaries/artifacts
4) KV-cache restores and ephemeral state
5) Worker autoscale/replica adjustments

Example pre-restore verification script (pseudo-bash embedded)

  #!/bin/bash
  set -euo pipefail
  ESCROW_DIR=$1
  # quick checksum validations
  jq -e . < ${ESCROW_DIR}/model-metadata.json || exit 2
  sha256sum -c ${ESCROW_DIR}/checksums.sha256 || exit 3
  echo "escrow bundle OK"

Handling partial failures and backout steps

- If escrow fetch fails: abort and notify the operator with cause. Do not proceed without verified escrow.
- If pre-restore verification fails: capture logs and mark incident as blocked; run rollback to a safe pause state (routing to prior safe variant) and create remediation ticket.
- If KV restore detects keyspace divergence > 0.5% relative to snapshot metadata: escalate to eng-platform for manual reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria for a successful rollback

- Synthetic acceptance tests show error rate <= baseline + 0.25% over 15 minutes.
- Latency p95 within 150% of baseline for 15 minutes.
- No token rejections observed in the same window.
- Operator evidence bundle uploaded to the incident ticket (escrow URI, operator-log, synthetic output).

Audit evidence and postmortem requirements

For every rollback performed under this playbook, collect and attach the following to the incident:

- Escrow URI and manifest (control-plane-manifest.yaml)
- Operator event log (operator-log-{change-id}.ndjson)
- Synthetic acceptance run results and raw traces
- Checksums and signature verification outputs
- A short timeline of operator actions (who did what and when)

Process-level automation hooks (operator sentinel integration)

- Sentinel should produce an event with these fields:
  - change_id, verdict (ok/degraded/unsafe), metrics_snapshot (p50/p95/errors/throughput), timestamp, operator_ns
- Automation rule: if verdict==unsafe -> call redwood operator rollback --change-id=... --mode=durable --auto-approve
- Automation must perform escrow validation and will fail if signatures are invalid; it will then pause and page operator.

Field operator playbook (quick steps)

1) Acknowledge the page; set Slack channel #private-rollbacks-ops.
2) Confirm sentinel verdict and change-id.
3) Run 'redwood operator escrow fetch'.
4) Run pre-restore validation.
5) Execute 'redwood operator rollback --change-id=... --mode=durable' (or follow manual steps if network constraints exist).
6) Run acceptance synthetics and confirm criteria.
7) Close the incident with attached evidence and schedule a follow-up RCA if the rollback was triggered by a regression.

Operator CLI examples (summary)

  redwood operator escrow create --change-id=chg-2026-1123 --escrow-uri=s3://... \
    --manifest=control-plane-manifest.yaml --operator=$USER

  redwood operator escrow fetch --change-id=chg-2026-1123 --dest=/tmp/chg-1123

  redwood operator rollback --change-id=chg-2026-1123 --mode=durable --timeout=1800

Testing and validation guidance

- Nightly synthetic runs must exercise rollback and restore paths in a non-production sandbox at least once per week for each major runtime version.
- Chaos test: simulate model swap failure with sentinel configured to mark unsafe and verify automation triggers rollback and evidence creation.

Operational metrics to export to dashboards

- escrow_creation_time (ms), escrow_validation_success{0/1}, rollback_duration_seconds, postrollback_slo_error_rate, rollback_attempts_count, kv_restore_success{0/1}

Owner maintenance tasks

- Platform Ops: review sentinel thresholds quarterly and after every major runtime release.
- Security/Compliance: quarterly audit of escrow storage ACLs and key rotation.
- Release engineering: ensure build pipeline produces signed escrow artifacts for every release.

Appendix: tenant quiesce template (API payload)

  {
    "tenant": "t-123",
    "change_id": "chg-2026-1123",
    "duration_s": 600,
    "reason": "rollback restore - kv snapshot restore",
    "operator_contact": "marceline@example.redwood.com"
  }

Appendix: minimal manifest example (control-plane-manifest.yaml snippet)

  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Deployment
  metadata:
    name: redwood-model-worker
    labels:
      app: rw-model
      change_id: chg-2026-1123
  spec:
    template:
      spec:
        containers:
          - name: worker
            image: registry.redwood.local/rw-model-worker:2026-03-22-commit-sha

Notes and future work

- We will extend the sentinel to collect lightweight model-quality signals (per-tenant hallucination detector) in 2027; this will feed into the unsafe decision earlier.
- Consider an escrow-tiering model for very large artifacts (multi-part escrow with manifest-only fastfail path).
